Christmas Eve Clear Beet Soup (Barszcz Wigilijny)

Served at: Christmas Eve

Serves 6-8Prep 25 minCook 1 hour 30 min

This vibrant, ruby-red clear beet soup, known as Barszcz Wigilijny, is a cherished centerpiece of the traditional Christmas Eve (Wigilia) supper in many Eastern European households. Meatless and deeply flavorful, its earthy sweetness and tangy notes symbolize warmth and good fortune, often served with tiny mushroom-filled dumplings called uszka.

Ingredients

  • 2 pounds (about 4-5 medium) fresh beets, scrubbed
  • 1 large onion, quartered
  • 2 carrots, roughly chopped
  • 1 parsnip, roughly chopped (optional)
  • 4 cups (1 liter) vegetable broth
  • 4 cups (1 liter) water
  • 1/2 ounce (15g) dried porcini or mixed wild mushrooms
  • 3 cloves garlic, smashed
  • 2 bay leaves
  • 5-6 allspice berries
  • 1 teaspoon salt, or to taste
  • 1/2 teaspoon black pepper, or to taste
  • 2-3 tablespoons (30-45ml) apple cider vinegar or fresh lemon juice, to taste
  • 1-2 teaspoons (5-10g) sugar, to taste (optional)
  • Fresh dill or parsley, for garnish (optional)

Method

  1. Rinse dried mushrooms thoroughly and place them in a small bowl with 1 cup (240ml) of hot water to rehydrate for at least 20 minutes.
  2. While mushrooms rehydrate, peel the beets and cut them into large chunks.
  3. In a large stockpot, combine the chopped beets, onion, carrots, parsnip (if using), garlic, bay leaves, and allspice berries.
  4. Add the vegetable broth and water to the pot, ensuring all vegetables are submerged. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 1 hour, or until the beets are very tender.
  5. Strain the rehydrated mushrooms, reserving the soaking liquid. Chop the rehydrated mushrooms finely. Add the chopped mushrooms and their strained soaking liquid (carefully, leaving any grit behind) to the simmering soup for the last 15 minutes of cooking.
  6. Once beets are tender, remove the pot from heat. Carefully strain the entire contents of the pot through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean bowl, pressing gently on the solids to extract all liquid. Discard the cooked vegetables and spices.
  7. Return the clear beet broth to the clean pot. Stir in salt, pepper, apple cider vinegar (or lemon juice), and sugar (if using). Taste and adjust seasonings as needed; the soup should be a balance of earthy, sweet, and tangy.
  8. Gently reheat the soup if needed before serving.

Tips

  • For an even deeper flavor, roast the beets before simmering them in the broth. This adds a lovely caramelized note.
  • Traditionally, this soup is served with small mushroom-filled dumplings called uszka, which are often added directly to each bowl.
  • If you prefer a richer, less clear soup, you can blend a small portion of the cooked beets back into the strained broth.
